title: GPM: Meet the Team: Lynette Marbley
description: This is a series of short profiles that showcase the systems engineers and designers who helped develop, build, and test the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) Core Observatory spacecraft.
keywords: GPM, Spacecraft, Japan, Testing, Engineers, Earth, JAXA
via: the NASA Image and Video Library

transcript.text: I've been at Goddard approximately 11 years. I've been on GPM for about three to four years.
I lead the quality assurance and the safety assurance team on GPM primarily for the instruments,
but I also have the role of that as well at the launch site.
When I first came on the project, I was working with Ball Aerospace on getting the GMI assembled
and shipped over here to Goddard. We went to a manufacturer to get the main reflector coated.
We saw there was stripes along the face of the main reflector, so we had to go, not only go back
and resurface it, but we actually had to remove that old surface to put on and prep it for a new surface.
When it finally came out and we finally saw it, we were like, wow, it was a pristine coating
exactly how we've seen it in the past in other projects and other dishes, and we were just ecstatic.
